chunks: The fifth is to aim at the flesh grown as a result of unlawful earning, so that you may melt it by grief (of repentance) till the skin touches the bone and a new flesh grows between them;

key_terms.الْأَحْزَانِ: Grief or sorrow (used here as the means of spiritual purification)
key_terms.لَحْمٌ جَدِيدٌ: New flesh (symbolizing the result of purified faith and body)

ai.seo_question: What is the fifth meaning of istighfār in Nahj al-Balagha regarding unlawful wealth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this metaphor illustrates the physical manifestation of spiritual impurity, where consuming *suh't* (unlawful wealth) causes the body to grow flesh derived specifically from that source. Sincere repentance (*tawbah*) acts as a transformative fire, melting away this impure flesh until the skin adheres to the bone, symbolizing the complete purification of the self. This process underscores the belief that true forgiveness requires not just verbal acknowledgment but a profound internal restructuring of one's being.
